name: quick: the dim line and the line then said, as the build is set (a draft may be shown from six words; a draft fits from half his words), with the clock stood in for. (1) Of three drafts the one that heard four words is never sent; the seven-word one is sent when written, the thirteen-word one is written after he lets go and is stamped after it: the app shows the seven-word line, and since its draft does not hear half of his 24 words the fixed line is said, with no other draft used, though the thirteen-word draft fits and is written. (2) The same hold, but the thirteen-word line is written before he lets go: it is the newest by the release, it fits, and it is the line said, ahead of nothing else. (3) A line too long to be said is not sent, so nothing is shown and the quick line is chosen as it always was: the first draft that fits. (4) A short question, no draft of six words: nothing is sent, and the quick line is chosen as it always was. (5) An older draft whose line is written after a newer one's has gone is not sent. (6) Two drafts fit his thirteen words and both lines are written before he lets go: the one shown is the newer, and it is the one said, where the older, written first, was said before this change
